svg.text: Packet anatomy — the four named contracts
Every crossing is a bounded packet with one ask, a scope boundary, and verifiable acceptance; none of them is "paste the repo"
Delegation Packet
Claude → worker · delegate-codex.sh submit
Context — why-forward
working on X for Y so that Z; never a
bare instruction with no purpose
Task
one clear sentence
Acceptance
commands or observable behaviour —
what the Phase 4 review judges against
Constraints
paths in and out of scope; no commit,
push, deploy, or secrets
Checkpoint rule
pause only for an irreversible action, a
real scope change, or user-only input
Output discipline
no optional commentary; at most three
lines of lessons for rollout memory
Nothing generates this packet
The driver composes it in its own
context, writes it to $(mktemp), and
passes the path. The script's only check
is that the file exists — this contract is
authorship discipline, not validation.
Routing is config, not prose
--role picks the identity; backend, model
and effort resolve from config and are
never restated inside the packet itself.
Fix rounds are thinner on purpose: the
findings, the failed criteria, and
"continue end-to-end from here".
E2E Packets
Claude → worker · submit --worktree, optional
Specification, inline
the frozen goal excerpt and the spec,
verbatim — a worktree has no .handoff/
Specifier task
Gherkin scenarios with stable IDs plus
tests in the stack it detected and names
Verifier task
run the reviewed tests against a pinned
commit; report what happened, do not
make it pass
Target
a named local or ephemeral target; a
remote or billable one is a hard stop
Constraints — replaced line
commit on this worktree branch; never
merge, push, rebase, or remove the tree
Verdict artifact
.handoff/e2e/<jobId>/verdict.json
Frozen · repairable · forbidden
Frozen: scenario text and IDs, expected
values, what an assertion is about.
Repairable: launch and runner
scaffolding, named in harness_edits.
Forbidden: product code — a failure is a
finding, not a bug the verifier fixes.
A semantic edit does not get disclosed
and accepted; it invalidates the run.
Whoever writes the assertions does not
decide whether they passed: specifier
writes, verifier runs, driver judges
the gate itself.
Goal Packet
Claude → user · authorization, opt-in protocol
Ask
one why-forward sentence: what was
asked for and why it matters
Plan
goal and non-goals · current-state
evidence as file:line, not vibes · file
scope · phases · risks · acceptance ·
rollback plan
Gate Verdict
which rows survived all three questions,
and what is already folded into the plan
Open Decisions
only what the user can decide — scope
tradeoffs, priorities, invisible constraints
What Authorization Unlocks
work up to merge-ready PR plus preview
verified — and explicitly nothing past it
A decision artifact, not a delegation
Sent before any branch, worktree, or
goal file exists: the plan stage touches
no files at all.
A reply that only answers a question in
the packet is not authorization. Wait for
an actual imperative.
One imperative, one action
Merge, production, tags, force-push,
deletion, destructive migration, and
external publish are each their own hard
stop, each needing its own fresh
sentence, recorded verbatim in the goal
file's Delivery.authorization field.
Spec Review Packet
Claude → deep_reasoner · planning, read-only, every plan
Context — why-forward
planning X for Y; the plan is about to go
to them, so read it before they do
Specification, inline
the goal line and its done_when, the task
table with acceptance, the design doc —
verbatim, never a path to go read
Task
review this plan and report what you
would change before any of it is built
Acceptance
prioritized findings, worst first · which
criteria are not verifiable as written ·
what is missing, not only what is wrong
Constraints — narrowed line
read-only: no file edited, no goal file
written, no product code touched
Output
no optional commentary; one line saying
the plan is sound beats invented findings
Once per run; declined blockers go to the arbiter at the cap
The goal file's Spec Review status is the marker: any status other than not run means the automatic review is spent for this run.
A resumed session finishes an open chain. The driver assesses findings; a declined blocking finding at the cap goes to the arbiter.
It is also the one packet that narrows this template rather than widening it: the e2e packets add a commit, this one removes every write.
Shared invariant
Each packet carries verifiable acceptance and states its scope boundary. The receiver is asked for prioritized findings against that acceptance,
not for a broad rewrite, and the sender stays accountable for the repository evidence it chose to include.
